issues: Most of the document breaks the 'each item one to three sentences' rule. Many items run four to seven sentences or are dense multi-clause blocks. Examples: part_02 Q1-C items 5, 12, 22 and 16–17; part_03 Q2-B items 19–22 and 24; part_03 Q2-C item 7; part_04 Q2-D items 4, 5, 10, 16 and 17; part_06 conduct A items 10, 16 and 17 and E items 1, 3, 5 and 8; part_07 Natera items 5 and 8, Caris item 6 and Tempus/GeneDx item 6; part_08 Roche items 3, 4, 10 and 17 and Element items 10 and 11; part_09 price-list items 1, 8, 10 and 13. These read as dense walls, not a readable list.

The same evidence is restated in several places, not merged into one item citing all its E-numbers. The 3.4x premium, the $728M clinical 6000 business, the ~$500M excess, the 47% hurdle, the 80–85% target and the 'dual owners' point recur in part_01 'The answer in brief', part_01 mechanics, part_02 sections A, B and F, the sizing table, part_04 section H, part_05 and part_10 bull/bear. Cross-reference items are also repeated in part_09 (Medicare, FDA, surveys, web pages) and part_08 section F. This inflates length and works against the 'merge near-duplicates' requirement.

part_01 'How the NovaSeq 6000-to-X conversion hits revenue: the mechanics' is mostly prose paragraphs, not a numbered, labelled evidence list. Its 'Why the conversion is not instant' and 'Why the 3.4x premium is larger than the list-price gap' paragraphs mix facts, former-employee hearsay, management phrases and our inference. They carry no per-statement Fact/Mgmt/Opinion/Our-calc labels, and the E-tags are bunched at the paragraph end. A reader cannot tell which claim is sourced to which tag.

Fact and opinion are blurred in places. Interpretive judgements are labelled *Fact*. Examples: 'Filings stopped naming the price cut', 'The over-earning question was deflected', 'The initial-price-hit question was deflected' and 'A mislabelled 91%' in part_01's conduct list; part_06 A items 14–15 on 'dropped' and 'softened' language; and part_06 B items 1–2 ('none got a number', 'sidestepped'). Whether a question was 'dodged' or a disclosure 'dropped' is the analyst's inference. These items should be labelled *Our calc/Opinion*, or split into a fact (what was asked and said) and an inference.

There is an unexplained denominator inconsistency in the headline sizing. part_01 Q1 item 3 and the sizing table say the $728M clinical 6000 business is ~36% of clinical sequencing consumables. The same sizing uses $2.17B for FY26 clinical, and 728/2,170 is about 33.5%. The ~23% figure for the $500M excess uses the $2.17B base. The ~36% figure presumably uses a different base (FY25?), but this is never stated. A reader checking the headline numbers will find they don't reconcile.

part_01 'Question 1' headline is hedged and conflates two things. It opens 'Probably yes' on a premium measured across all HT customers, then applies it to clinical by assumption. 'Over-earning' is never defined up front, and the yardstick is only implied by 'if priced like X Gb'. The stock-versus-flow distinction ($0.5B excess vs $150–190M a year unwound) is only fully explained later in part_02's Sizing section, so the answer is not fully clear at the point of the headline.

Several terms are used without a plain-English gloss at first use. CEA (part_04 B item 16, 'same frequency as CEA monitoring'), atezolizumab and IMvigor011 (part_04 B items 12–13), WGS-MRD (part_11 watch table), 'Medicare Part B' (part_04 B item 25), CLIA (part_01 mechanics, named only in passing), EY (part_07 D item 17), and 'IVD' (used in part_01 before part_02 defines it). Some terms are defined only later than first use, for example RUO (part_08) and 10b5-1. This breaks the 'explain each piece of jargon the first time' rule.

Some model and walk-through steps carry no ledger tag. In part_05 'A walk-through in words', step 4 has none, and the 'Mix' and 'Price' bullets are tagged only loosely. The part_01 mechanics 'arithmetic' bullets carry no tags of their own. Spec item 5 requires every evidence item to carry its tag.

part_01 'Management conduct and credibility' (the brief) is only a 14-line list of one-liners. The fuller conduct section (part_06) is spread over five sub-sections with 'Severity/relevance' labels that are not defined in the part_01 'How to read' legend, which lists only Fact/Mgmt/Opinion/Our calc. The severity and relevance ratings are themselves judgement calls, but are not marked as opinion.

part_06 opens with a dense summary paragraph that cites section letters and item numbers in shorthand ('B1 and B3, plus Question 1, section C, item 5'; '(C3, C5)'; '(E1, E5)'). These references are hard to follow, and 'E1, E5' collides visually with ledger tags like [E001]. The conduct 'short answer' is not written in plain lead-with-the-answer style.

part_06 sections D and E contain many low-relevance items (SEC comment letters, tax-rate notes, legal-chief severance, Glassdoor ratings, board turnover, DSO and CVR accounting detail) given equal list weight. They are rated 'relevance low' by the document itself. This dilutes the readable-list quality and buries the material items, which are metrics and dodges. The spec asks for breadth, but not for undifferentiated volume without prioritisation.

part_02 and part_03 mix 'Mgmt', 'Fact' and 'Our calc' inside single items without separating them. Examples: part_02 Q1-A items 6 and 7; Q1-B items 7 and 12; Q1-C items 8 and 9, labelled 'Mgmt + fact' or 'Mgmt + our calc'. A reader cannot tell which clause is the management claim and which is our arithmetic. This weakens the fact/claim/opinion distinction the spec requires.

Several figures lack a clear comparison or why-it-matters. Examples: part_04 Q2-B item 8 ('Veracyte 17%, BillionToOne 35%, Myriad −1%' with no baseline); part_04 item 27 (MolDX coverage-policy dates with no sizing); part_03 Q1-B item 13 and item 14 pull-through percentages. Several price-card dollar figures in part_09 items 7, 10 and 14 are listed with no stated takeaway beyond 'direction'. This drifts toward number vomit.

The 'Where sources disagree' section (part_11) mixes consequential disagreements with trivial ones. Item 13 on insider totals and item 14's list of seven unrelated competitor mismatches are source-error nits. They take space from the disagreements that matter. Item 14 also nests bullets under a numbered item, which is inconsistent with the rest of the list format.

part_11 'How this addendum was built' is long and mixes a process narrative with an agent-number inventory ('Agents 01–17... agents 21 to 144, about 31 waves'). It carries internal working-file names (13_, 52_, 45_, 18_). These file names are also leaked into part_01's 'Our three models', so the section does not fully stand alone for a reader without the working folder.

part_03 Q1-F and part_05 present near-identical scenario results in several overlapping tables (revenue-at-risk bridge, the model's 'excess unwound', part_04 H hurdle table, the part_03 two-year break-even table). Their different base assumptions (constant Gb, volume uplift, 15% extra volume, different conversion paths) make the headline flow figures ($150–190M, $165M, $190M, $240M) hard to reconcile. The reconciliation is given in only one dense paragraph (part_02, Sizing).

part_04 Q2-H second table and its commentary lean on a 'time basis' mix (trailing vs forward vs superseded model) and call the base case 'a deliberate slowdown'. The slowdown assumption (+30%/+26% Gb) is a judgement, but the table puts it among evidence. The verdict paragraph then says volume 'offsets the price decline' for 2027–28 while the same page shows the base case barely offsets (+2.5%), so the Q2 answer reads as both 'yes' and 'barely' without a crisp bottom line.

Sell-side and stock-price material in part_10 ('Where the Street and the stock stand', items 1–14) is only loosely tied to the two thesis questions. It includes short interest, option-implied moves and customer stock moves. This is breadth, but it is not organised around implications for the thesis. Only a one-line sentence says what each figure implies, in the section intro.

part_09 'Alternative data' is mostly cross-reference stubs ('Cross-reference. Fact. The payer evidence is set out in full in...'). These items carry ledger tags but add no new evidence. Their 'Fact' labels are misleading, since they are pointers, not facts.

Weak-source flags are applied inconsistently. Some weak items are flagged inline (Signatera Genome spec, GRAIL expiry). Others are asserted flatly in the headline lists, such as the 'Caris 10-K mentions both platforms' summary and the NHS genome volumes (flagged only in the item). The part_11 'Weak evidence' list says none is load-bearing, but the GRAIL renewal date appears in the watch-table as a dated event.
